subject: LANGUAGE
title: Sentence structures: prove the clauses
goal: Define, identify and construct sentence structures by clause evidence—not length, commas or the presence of and.
teach: A clause contains a subject and a verb working together. An independent clause can communicate a complete statement. A dependent clause has that subject–verb structure but relies on another clause, often because a word such as although or because makes it incomplete alone.

Count clause types: simple = 1 independent, 0 dependent; compound = 2 or more independent, 0 dependent; complex = 1 independent, 1 or more dependent; compound-complex = 2 or more independent, 1 or more dependent.
Two verbs do not automatically make two clauses. “The artist sketched and painted” has one subject doing two actions in one independent clause. A long sentence can still be simple.

Test each proposed independent clause by reading it alone. Then identify any dependent clause and its subject/verb. Words such as after can begin a phrase (“after lunch”) or a clause (“after lunch ended”); inspect the structure.

Use sentence structure to express relationships: equal ideas can be coordinated; a cause, condition or time relationship can be subordinated. Classification must follow the actual sentence, not the relationship you intended.
Find subject and verb. Test alone. Mark I or D. Count, then name.

A dependent clause can sit inside a sentence: Mia wondered why the fabric shrank. The main clause is Mia wondered; why the fabric shrank is an embedded dependent clause. The sentence is complex even though it does not begin with because or although.

model.prompt: Although the first seam tore, Mira repaired it, and the jacket fit.
steps: “Although the first seam tore”: subject seam, verb tore; although makes this dependent.
“Mira repaired it”: subject Mira, verb repaired; complete independent clause.
“The jacket fit”: subject jacket, verb fit; complete independent clause.
Count 2 independent + 1 dependent → compound-complex. The word and alone was not sufficient proof.
model.reasoning: “Although the first seam tore”: subject seam, verb tore; although makes this dependent. “Mira repaired it”: subject Mira, verb repaired; complete independent clause. “The jacket fit”: subject jacket, verb fit; complete independent clause. Count 2 independent + 1 dependent → compound-complex. The word and alone was not sufficient proof.

guided.prompt: The musician practiced scales and played a new melody. Mark the subject, verbs and clause count.
guided.expected: Subject musician; verbs practiced and played; one independent clause, no dependent clause; simple.
guided.support: Ask whether “played a new melody” supplies its own subject. It shares musician rather than creating a second clause.

practice.prompt: The designer measured the fabric and cut the lining. Choose the structure and proof.
options: Complex: lining is a dependent clause.
Compound: and always joins two independent clauses.
Simple: one independent clause with a compound predicate; no dependent clause.
Compound-complex: two actions mean two independent and one dependent clause.
practice.correctAnswer: Simple: one independent clause with a compound predicate; no dependent clause.
practice.rationale: Designer is the shared subject of measured and cut; no additional subject–verb clause is introduced.

repair.prompt: At sunrise, the hikers packed their bags and checked the trail. Which structure and clause count are accurate?
options: Simple: 1 independent clause and 0 dependent clauses.
Complex: 1 independent clause and 1 dependent clause.
Compound-complex: 2 independent clauses and 1 dependent clause.
Compound: 2 independent clauses and 0 dependent clauses.
repair.rationale: The hikers share packed and checked; at sunrise is a phrase. Count: 1 independent, 0 dependent.
repair.teach: Work through the saved response first. Designer is the shared subject of measured and cut; no additional subject–verb clause is introduced. Explain which condition or evidence supports that answer; then try the different example below.

practice.prompt: The capybara rested, and the birds watched. Choose the structure and proof.
options: Complex: and makes the second clause dependent.
Compound: “the capybara rested” and “the birds watched” can each stand alone.
Compound-complex: every comma signals a dependent clause.
Simple: both clauses mention animals.
practice.correctAnswer: Compound: “the capybara rested” and “the birds watched” can each stand alone.
practice.rationale: Two independent clauses, no dependent clause: compound.

repair.prompt: Zoe sketched the mural, and Omar mixed the paint. Which structure and clause count are accurate?
options: Compound: 2 independent clauses and 0 dependent clauses.
Compound-complex: 2 independent clauses and 1 dependent clause.
Complex: 1 independent clause and 1 dependent clause.
Simple: 1 independent clause and 0 dependent clauses.
repair.rationale: Zoe sketched and Omar mixed each form an independent clause. Count: 2 independent, 0 dependent.
repair.teach: Work through the saved response first. Two independent clauses, no dependent clause: compound. Explain which condition or evidence supports that answer; then try the different example below.

practice.prompt: Because the soil was dry, the class watered the garden. Choose the structure and proof.
options: Compound: any two subject–verb groups are independent.
Compound-complex: because always adds two independent clauses.
Complex: one dependent because-clause and one independent clause.
Simple: the sentence has only one period.
practice.correctAnswer: Complex: one dependent because-clause and one independent clause.
practice.rationale: “Because the soil was dry” depends on a main statement; “the class watered the garden” stands alone.

repair.prompt: Because the path was flooded, the hikers took a detour. Which structure and clause count are accurate?
options: Compound: 2 independent clauses and 0 dependent clauses.
Complex: 1 independent clause and 1 dependent clause.
Compound-complex: 2 independent clauses and 1 dependent clause.
Simple: 1 independent clause and 0 dependent clauses.
repair.rationale: Because the path was flooded is dependent; the hikers took a detour is independent. Count: 1 independent, 1 dependent.
repair.teach: Work through the saved response first. “Because the soil was dry” depends on a main statement; “the class watered the garden” stands alone. Explain which condition or evidence supports that answer; then try the different example below.

practice.prompt: When the rehearsal ended, Ava packed her music, and Eli closed the piano. Choose the structure and proof.
options: Complex: every sentence beginning with when has only one independent clause.
Simple: the actions all happen at rehearsal.
Compound: when is only a decoration.
Compound-complex: one dependent time clause and two independent clauses.
practice.correctAnswer: Compound-complex: one dependent time clause and two independent clauses.
practice.rationale: When-clause is dependent; Ava packed and Eli closed are distinct independent clauses.

repair.prompt: While the pasta cooled, Ben set the table, and Ava poured the drinks. Which structure and clause count are accurate?
options: Simple: 1 independent clause and 0 dependent clauses.
Compound-complex: 2 independent clauses and 1 dependent clause.
Compound: 2 independent clauses and 0 dependent clauses.
Complex: 1 independent clause and 1 dependent clause.
repair.rationale: While the pasta cooled is dependent; Ben set and Ava poured are independent clauses. Count: 2 independent, 1 dependent.
repair.teach: Work through the saved response first. When-clause is dependent; Ava packed and Eli closed are distinct independent clauses. Explain which condition or evidence supports that answer; then try the different example below.

practice.prompt: After the art show, the judges discussed color and texture. Which claim is accurate?
options: Compound-complex: judges is plural.
Compound: color and texture are independent clauses.
Complex: after always begins a clause.
Simple: “after the art show” is a phrase, not a subject–verb clause.
practice.correctAnswer: Simple: “after the art show” is a phrase, not a subject–verb clause.
practice.rationale: The opening phrase has no verb paired with art show; the main clause is the only clause.

repair.prompt: During the rehearsal, the singers warmed up quietly. Which structure and clause count are accurate?
options: Compound: 2 independent clauses and 0 dependent clauses.
Simple: 1 independent clause and 0 dependent clauses.
Complex: 1 independent clause and 1 dependent clause.
Compound-complex: 2 independent clauses and 1 dependent clause.
repair.rationale: During the rehearsal is a phrase without a subject-verb pair; the main statement is one independent clause. Count: 1 independent, 0 dependent.
repair.teach: Work through the saved response first. The opening phrase has no verb paired with art show; the main clause is the only clause. Explain which condition or evidence supports that answer; then try the different example below.

practice.prompt: The plants wilted; the students checked the irrigation. Which proof fits?
options: Simple: no coordinating conjunction means no compound sentence.
Compound-complex: a semicolon creates a dependent clause.
Complex: irrigation is a dependent clause.
Compound: two independent clauses joined with a semicolon.
practice.correctAnswer: Compound: two independent clauses joined with a semicolon.
practice.rationale: Independent clauses need not be joined by and; each stated clause has its own subject and verb.

repair.prompt: The timer rang; the cooks removed the bread. Which structure and clause count are accurate?
options: Complex: 1 independent clause and 1 dependent clause.
Compound-complex: 2 independent clauses and 1 dependent clause.
Simple: 1 independent clause and 0 dependent clauses.
Compound: 2 independent clauses and 0 dependent clauses.
repair.rationale: The timer rang and the cooks removed the bread stand alone and are joined with a semicolon. Count: 2 independent, 0 dependent.
repair.teach: Work through the saved response first. Independent clauses need not be joined by and; each stated clause has its own subject and verb. Explain which condition or evidence supports that answer; then try the different example below.

practice.prompt: The friends changed their plan because the forecast predicted rain. Which proof fits?
options: Compound: forecast is another independent sentence by itself.
Complex: one independent clause plus a dependent because-clause, even though the dependent clause comes last.
Simple: a dependent clause must come first.
Compound-complex: because means there are at least two independent clauses.
practice.correctAnswer: Complex: one independent clause plus a dependent because-clause, even though the dependent clause comes last.
practice.rationale: Clause function is unchanged by its position.

repair.prompt: The librarian saved the book because Theo requested it. Which structure and clause count are accurate?
options: Simple: 1 independent clause and 0 dependent clauses.
Compound-complex: 2 independent clauses and 1 dependent clause.
Compound: 2 independent clauses and 0 dependent clauses.
Complex: 1 independent clause and 1 dependent clause.
repair.rationale: The librarian saved the book is independent; because Theo requested it is dependent. Count: 1 independent, 1 dependent.
repair.teach: Work through the saved response first. Clause function is unchanged by its position. Explain which condition or evidence supports that answer; then try the different example below.

practice.prompt: Although the budget was small, the club bought supplies; the volunteers donated fabric. Which proof fits?
options: Compound: semicolons erase dependent clauses.
Compound-complex: one dependent clause and two independent clauses.
Complex: every sentence beginning with although has exactly one independent clause.
Simple: the sentence is about one club.
practice.correctAnswer: Compound-complex: one dependent clause and two independent clauses.
practice.rationale: Count all clauses: although budget was small (D); club bought supplies (I); volunteers donated fabric (I).

repair.prompt: Although the first battery failed, the lamp stayed on, for a second battery supplied power. Which structure and clause count are accurate?
options: Simple: 1 independent clause and 0 dependent clauses.
Complex: 1 independent clause and 1 dependent clause.
Compound: 2 independent clauses and 0 dependent clauses.
Compound-complex: 2 independent clauses and 1 dependent clause.
repair.rationale: Although the first battery failed is dependent. The lamp stayed on and a second battery supplied power are independent; for coordinates them. Count: 2 independent, 1 dependent.
repair.teach: Work through the saved response first. Count all clauses: although budget was small (D); club bought supplies (I); volunteers donated fabric (I). Explain which condition or evidence supports that answer; then try the different example below.

practice.prompt: Choose exactly TWO sentences with exactly one independent clause and no dependent clause.
options: Although the paint dried, the canvas remained sticky.
The artist sketched and shaded the portrait.
The group planned, and the teacher listened.
After lunch, the group planned the exhibit.
practice.rationale: A compound predicate can remain one clause; after lunch is a phrase. Although introduces a dependent clause; the last sentence has two independent clauses.

repair.prompt: Before breakfast, the dog stretched and yawned. Which structure and clause count are accurate?
options: Complex: 1 independent clause and 1 dependent clause.
Simple: 1 independent clause and 0 dependent clauses.
Compound-complex: 2 independent clauses and 1 dependent clause.
Compound: 2 independent clauses and 0 dependent clauses.
repair.rationale: Before breakfast is a phrase; the dog shares the two verbs in one independent clause. Count: 1 independent, 0 dependent.
repair.teach: Work through the saved response first. A compound predicate can remain one clause; after lunch is a phrase. Although introduces a dependent clause; the last sentence has two independent clauses. Explain which condition or evidence supports that answer; then try the different example below.

independentCheck.prompt: During the storm, the campers stayed inside and played cards. Choose the structure and proof.
options: Simple: one independent clause, no dependent clause; during the storm is a phrase.
Compound-complex: campers is plural.
Compound: two actions automatically make two clauses.
Complex: during the storm has a subject and verb.
independentCheck.correctAnswer: Simple: one independent clause, no dependent clause; during the storm is a phrase.
independentCheck.rationale: The campers share stayed and played. During the storm has no subject–verb pair.

repair.prompt: Near the window, the seedlings grew rapidly and leaned toward the light. Which structure and clause count are accurate?
options: Complex: 1 independent clause and 1 dependent clause.
Compound: 2 independent clauses and 0 dependent clauses.
Simple: 1 independent clause and 0 dependent clauses.
Compound-complex: 2 independent clauses and 1 dependent clause.
repair.rationale: The seedlings share grew and leaned. Neither opening nor ending prepositional phrase adds a clause. Count: 1 independent, 0 dependent.
repair.teach: Work through the saved response first. The campers share stayed and played. During the storm has no subject–verb pair. Explain which condition or evidence supports that answer; then try the different example below.

independentCheck.prompt: The recipe looked easy, but the dough needed more time. Choose the structure and proof.
options: Complex: but makes the second clause dependent.
Compound: two independent clauses, no dependent clause.
Simple: only one recipe is discussed.
Compound-complex: needed more time is a third dependent clause.
independentCheck.correctAnswer: Compound: two independent clauses, no dependent clause.
independentCheck.rationale: Recipe looked easy and dough needed more time each supplies a complete statement.

repair.prompt: Jules counted the tickets, but Erin checked the names. Which structure and clause count are accurate?
options: Simple: 1 independent clause and 0 dependent clauses.
Complex: 1 independent clause and 1 dependent clause.
Compound-complex: 2 independent clauses and 1 dependent clause.
Compound: 2 independent clauses and 0 dependent clauses.
repair.rationale: Jules counted and Erin checked are separate independent subject-verb units. Count: 2 independent, 0 dependent.
repair.teach: Work through the saved response first. Recipe looked easy and dough needed more time each supplies a complete statement. Explain which condition or evidence supports that answer; then try the different example below.

independentCheck.prompt: The club postponed the picnic because the field was flooded. Choose the structure and proof.
options: Simple: the cause comes last.
Compound: the word field is a complete clause.
Complex: one independent clause and one dependent because-clause.
Compound-complex: a because-clause always adds two independent clauses.
independentCheck.correctAnswer: Complex: one independent clause and one dependent because-clause.
independentCheck.rationale: The club postponed the picnic is independent; because the field was flooded depends on that main clause.

repair.prompt: Since the stage was ready, the actors began. Which structure and clause count are accurate?
options: Simple: 1 independent clause and 0 dependent clauses.
Compound: 2 independent clauses and 0 dependent clauses.
Compound-complex: 2 independent clauses and 1 dependent clause.
Complex: 1 independent clause and 1 dependent clause.
repair.rationale: Since the stage was ready is a dependent clause; the actors began stands alone. Count: 1 independent, 1 dependent.
repair.teach: Work through the saved response first. The club postponed the picnic is independent; because the field was flooded depends on that main clause. Explain which condition or evidence supports that answer; then try the different example below.

independentCheck.prompt: If the weather improves, we will meet outside, and our teacher will bring the maps. Choose the structure and proof.
options: Complex: any sentence with if has exactly one independent clause.
Compound-complex: the if-clause is dependent, and the two following clauses are independent.
Simple: the whole sentence describes one plan.
Compound: if is never part of a clause.
independentCheck.correctAnswer: Compound-complex: the if-clause is dependent, and the two following clauses are independent.
independentCheck.rationale: Weather improves forms a dependent condition; we will meet and teacher will bring are independent subject–verb units.

repair.prompt: If the bus arrives early, we can visit the museum, and our guide can show us the exhibit. Which structure and clause count are accurate?
options: Compound: 2 independent clauses and 0 dependent clauses.
Compound-complex: 2 independent clauses and 1 dependent clause.
Simple: 1 independent clause and 0 dependent clauses.
Complex: 1 independent clause and 1 dependent clause.
repair.rationale: If the bus arrives early is dependent; we can visit and our guide can show are independent clauses. Count: 2 independent, 1 dependent.
repair.teach: Work through the saved response first. Weather improves forms a dependent condition; we will meet and teacher will bring are independent subject–verb units. Explain which condition or evidence supports that answer; then try the different example below.

proof.prompt: Write one simple, one compound, one complex and one compound-complex sentence about organizing a fashion show. For each, mark every clause I or D, identify its subject and verb, state I/D counts, and explain one relationship expressed. Do not use the model sentences.
criteria: All four structures match their definitions
Every clause is accurately bounded with subject and verb
I/D counts justify each classification
At least one sentence intentionally expresses an accurate cause, condition, contrast or time relationship

delayed.prompt: The painter mixed blue and yellow paint. Structure and proof?
options: Simple: one independent clause; blue and yellow are not two clauses.
Complex: yellow paint is dependent.
Compound: and always creates two clauses.
Compound-complex: two colors create two independent clauses.
delayed.correctAnswer: Simple: one independent clause; blue and yellow are not two clauses.
delayed.rationale: Only painter mixed supplies a subject–verb clause.

repair.prompt: The fox slept beneath a fallen tree. Which structure and clause count are accurate?
options: Compound: 2 independent clauses and 0 dependent clauses.
Compound-complex: 2 independent clauses and 1 dependent clause.
Simple: 1 independent clause and 0 dependent clauses.
Complex: 1 independent clause and 1 dependent clause.
repair.rationale: The fox slept is the only subject-verb clause; beneath a fallen tree is a phrase. Count: 1 independent, 0 dependent.
repair.teach: Work through the saved response first. Only painter mixed supplies a subject–verb clause. Explain which condition or evidence supports that answer; then try the different example below.

delayed.prompt: The power failed; the musicians continued without microphones. Structure and proof?
options: Compound-complex: microphones is plural.
Complex: without microphones is a dependent clause.
Simple: a semicolon removes a clause.
Compound: two independent clauses and no dependent clause.
delayed.correctAnswer: Compound: two independent clauses and no dependent clause.
delayed.rationale: Power failed and musicians continued can each stand alone; without microphones is a phrase.

repair.prompt: Mina sharpened her pencil; Luis opened the atlas. Which structure and clause count are accurate?
options: Simple: 1 independent clause and 0 dependent clauses.
Compound: 2 independent clauses and 0 dependent clauses.
Complex: 1 independent clause and 1 dependent clause.
Compound-complex: 2 independent clauses and 1 dependent clause.
repair.rationale: Mina sharpened and Luis opened form two independent clauses; neither is subordinated. Count: 2 independent, 0 dependent.
repair.teach: Work through the saved response first. Power failed and musicians continued can each stand alone; without microphones is a phrase. Explain which condition or evidence supports that answer; then try the different example below.

delayed.prompt: Although the directions were brief, the diagram clarified the process. Structure and proof?
options: Complex: a dependent although-clause plus one independent clause.
Simple: brief directions create simple sentences.
Compound: the comma makes both parts independent.
Compound-complex: although creates two independent clauses.
delayed.correctAnswer: Complex: a dependent although-clause plus one independent clause.
delayed.rationale: Although directions were brief depends on the independent diagram clarified statement.

repair.prompt: When the soil warmed, the seeds sprouted. Which structure and clause count are accurate?
options: Complex: 1 independent clause and 1 dependent clause.
Simple: 1 independent clause and 0 dependent clauses.
Compound: 2 independent clauses and 0 dependent clauses.
Compound-complex: 2 independent clauses and 1 dependent clause.
repair.rationale: When the soil warmed depends on the independent statement the seeds sprouted. Count: 1 independent, 1 dependent.
repair.teach: Work through the saved response first. Although directions were brief depends on the independent diagram clarified statement. Explain which condition or evidence supports that answer; then try the different example below.

delayed.prompt: When the doors opened, the audience entered, but the performers waited backstage. Structure and proof?
options: Compound: when never marks dependence.
Complex: but prevents a second independent clause.
Simple: this is one event.
Compound-complex: one dependent time clause and two independent clauses.
delayed.correctAnswer: Compound-complex: one dependent time clause and two independent clauses.
delayed.rationale: When doors opened is dependent; audience entered and performers waited are independent.

repair.prompt: Because the road was icy, the driver slowed down, and the passengers fastened their belts. Which structure and clause count are accurate?
options: Complex: 1 independent clause and 1 dependent clause.
Compound-complex: 2 independent clauses and 1 dependent clause.
Compound: 2 independent clauses and 0 dependent clauses.
Simple: 1 independent clause and 0 dependent clauses.
repair.rationale: The because-clause is dependent; the driver slowed and the passengers fastened form independent clauses. Count: 2 independent, 1 dependent.
repair.teach: Work through the saved response first. When doors opened is dependent; audience entered and performers waited are independent. Explain which condition or evidence supports that answer; then try the different example below.

checks.prompt: Explain one connection above. What stays the same, and what changes?
checks.review: Requires a named concept and accurate relationship, not just two subject names.

checks.prompt: Give a different situation where this idea would help. Explain the evidence that makes the connection valid.
checks.review: Requires a fresh application and a valid limit; teacher/parent review, not keyword scoring.

bridge.prompt: In “Although the fabric shrank, Maya finished the bag,” which group could stand alone? Explain why.
bridge.explanation: “Maya finished the bag” is an independent clause. “Although the fabric shrank” has a subject and verb but depends on another clause. One independent plus one dependent clause makes a complex sentence.

links.laterApplication: Use this idea again without notes after 1, 3, 7, 14 and 30 days. Explain a new example and a limit; familiar wording alone does not prove understanding.

memoryTactic.title: Count before naming
memoryTactic.text: Find subject and verb. Test alone. Mark I or D. Count, then name.
memoryTactic.limit: A useful cue only; a label without clause proof is not mastery.

game.title: Clause Architect
game.directions: Build sentence cards from independent/dependent clause tiles. Choose a target structure; construct it, then defend I/D counts. Add a decoy phrase tile so marker words alone cannot reveal the answer.

media.title: Identifying Independent and Dependent Clauses
media.task: Read the independent/dependent definitions and connecting-clause section. Use original app tiles to sort a complete clause, a dependent clause and a phrase; identify the subject and verb rather than sorting by word length. Close the resource: Close the reference. Explain the difference between a phrase and a dependent clause and prove the classification of an original sentence. New application: Classify: “After the performance, the musicians packed their instruments and thanked the audience.” Then revise it to include a dependent clause and show I/D counts.

verification.content: Full main explanation read, including connecting clauses and common errors

omissions: Reference is written for a broad audience; app supplies short chunks and original examples
Clause definitions alone do not prove mastery of all four sentence structures

retentionProofs.prompt: Without the cheat sheet, write one simple sentence with two actions and one compound sentence about a piano rehearsal. Mark each clause’s subject/verb and prove I/D counts. Explain why two actions alone do not prove compound.
criteria: Simple example has one I and no D
Compound example has at least two I and no D
Subjects/verbs and boundaries accurate
Explains shared-subject compound predicate distinction

retentionProofs.prompt: Use this new information: the fabric arrived late; the group changed its plan. Write one complex and one compound sentence expressing the relationship. Mark I/D and explain how your structural choices change emphasis.
criteria: Complex has one I and at least one D
Compound has two I and no D
Clause marking supports labels
Meaning/emphasis comparison accurate

retentionProofs.prompt: Create a compound-complex sentence about a garden under changing weather. Then remove or revise one clause to make a complex sentence. Show I/D counts before and after and explain the effect.
criteria: Original has at least two I and one D
Revision has exactly one I and at least one D
Clause counts/boundaries accurate
Explains the structural change without counting commas as clauses

retentionProofs.prompt: A long project instruction includes after lunch, two verbs sharing a subject, and no other subject–verb pair. Explain its possible sentence type. Then construct a different sentence beginning after lunch ended and prove what changes.
criteria: Distinguishes phrase after lunch from clause after lunch ended
Explains shared-subject two-action structure
New example contains accurate dependent/main structure
Labels follow actual counts rather than length or marker alone

proofRepair.prompt: Read these new sentences: (1) After the final bell, the volunteers stacked chairs and swept the floor. (2) After the final bell rang, the volunteers stacked chairs, and the custodian locked the doors. For each, mark every clause’s subject and verb, label I or D, give the counts, and name the structure. Explain why adding a subject–verb pair after after changes the opening from a phrase to a clause. Finally revise sentence 2 into a complex sentence and prove its new counts.
criteria: Sentence 1 correctly classified simple with one I and no D; its opening is a phrase
Sentence 2 correctly classified compound-complex with two I and one D
Subject–verb evidence and clause boundaries are accurate
Original revision has exactly one I and at least one D, with correct justification
proofRepair.teachingBeforePractice: Model with a different pair: “During the break, Noor stretched and drank water” versus “While the break continued, Noor stretched.” Identify the subject–verb unit, test whether it can stand alone, and count before applying a label. Remind Riley that two actions sharing a subject need not create two independent clauses.
proofRepair.reviewNotes: Do not auto-pass a correct label without the clause proof. Accept different valid revisions that satisfy the requested structure; the exact model wording is not required.
